analysis.title: Chart of the Week: Fed rate hikes challenge core fixed income
key_insights: The Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate Bond Index fell 3.5% in Q3 2026 as resilient economic data, persistent inflation and high energy prices pushed Treasury yields sharply higher.
Since late 2017 the Agg has returned -4.1% annualized during Fed hiking cycles, versus 3.3% when the Fed held rates steady and about 4.3% during easing cycles.
The Fed is expected to hold at next week's meeting, but markets are pricing two to three hikes over the next 12 months.
Further tightening complicates the outlook for core fixed income. Higher yields provide more income, but rate uncertainty leaves the path for total returns less certain.

macro_indicators.reading: Two to three hikes priced over the next 12 months
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing implies further tightening, which has historically meant negative annualized returns for core bonds.
A hold is the base case, so the pressure on bonds comes from the pricing of later hikes.

macro_indicators.indicator: Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate Bond Index Q3 return
macro_indicators.interpretation: Core bonds lost value as Treasury yields rose sharply on resilient data, persistent inflation and high energy prices.

risk_factors: Persistent inflation and high energy prices keep upward pressure on Treasury yields.
Continued rate uncertainty makes total returns on core fixed income less certain even with higher income.
